source.citation: Xu, T., Spycher, N., Sonnenthal, E., Zheng, L., Pruess, K. (2012). TOUGHREACT User's Guide: A Simulation Program for Non-isothermal Multiphase Reactive Transport in Variably Saturated Geologic Media, Version 2.0. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, LBNL-DRAFT, October 2012.

transcription.from: the report (PDF from tough.lbl.gov), Table H.1-1, p. 218
transcription.note: The package attributed these radii to Table A2 of Xu et al. (2011), the Computers & Geosciences article on TOUGHREACT V2; that article has no such table and no ionic radii. They are the radii this user's guide assigns, by charge, to species absent from Table 3 of Helgeson et al. (1981), and agree with it to the last digit.

rows: rounded average of the CO3-- and SO4-- values
estimated from a straight-line fit with charge
rounded average for the +2 species of HKF Table 3
rounded average for the +3 species of HKF Table 3
estimated with HKF Equation 142 and the average crystallographic radii of +4 species in the CRC Handbook

notes: Effective electrostatic radii r_e,j in Angstrom. TOUGHREACT does not use them as ion-size parameters directly: it forms a_j = 2 (r_e,j + 1.91 |z_j|) / (|z_j| + 1) for anions and the same with 1.81 for cations (Eqs. H.4-H.5, the NaCl-dominated form of HKF Eq. 125).
